newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - KOOR TRADES AT BIG DISCOUNT.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - KOOR TRADES AT BIG DISCOUNT.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries Ltd is trading at an excessive 25 percent discount to its net asset value, Ilanot Betucha Investment House Ltd said on Sunday.
"The gap between the value of Koor's holdings and its market value at which its traded at today is big and does not correctly reflect the operations and state of the company," Ilanot said.

It attributed the discount to the market's concerns about lower profitability in Koor's key businesses in telecommunications equipment (Telrad Electronic Telecommunications and Industries and Tadiran Ltd) and building products (Nesher Cement).

"An analysis by Ilanot Discount shows that in 1997-98 the company is expected to be hurt by a downturn in profitability at Telrad and Tadiran due to a drop in demand and price for their products from Bezeq," Ilanot said.
Bezeq Israel Telecom, Israel's main telecommunications company, is winding up a major investment programme and is reducing orders for switching equipment from the two Koor-controlled companies.
Ilanot said it expected Koor to offset the downturns by stepped-up exports.

Ilanot Discount said it expects Koor's net earnings to decline to about 530 million shekels in 1997, including approximately 190 million shekels in capital gains, from about 603 million shekels last year.
Nevertheless, it said, Koor was trading at an "unjustifiably" low prospective 1997 price-to-earnings ratio of 8.9.
